name: The Godfather
hook: A 1972 Best Picture winner whose lines, cast, and family saga Jeopardy keeps returning to.

facts.label: Mario Puzo
facts.statement: Mario Puzo wrote the 1969 novel, prompted by needing money for his five children; Francis Ford Coppola co-wrote and directed the 1972 film.

facts.label: Marlon Brando
facts.statement: Marlon Brando played Vito Corleone, the don whose offer you can't refuse; Puzo wrote to him saying he was the only actor for the part.

facts.label: Al Pacino
facts.statement: Al Pacino played Michael Corleone in all three films, including the kiss for his betraying brother Fredo in Part II.

facts.label: 1972 Best Picture
facts.statement: The Godfather won the 1972 Best Picture Oscar; it and its sequel are tied with On the Waterfront at three Best Supporting Actor nominations each.

facts.label: Talia Shire and Sofia Coppola
facts.statement: Francis Ford Coppola cast his sister Talia Shire as Connie and his daughter Sofia as the infant baptized in the first film; Sofia later played Michael's daughter Mary in Part III.

facts.label: The Godfather Part III
facts.statement: Part III sends Michael to Sicily for Cavalleria rusticana, introduces Andy Garcia as Vincent Mancini, and gives the line "friendship and money — oil and water."
